definitions.meaning: neat is an old word for cattle, and an ... is one of a breed of dairy cattle
one of the Channel Islands between England and France

explanation.surface: A tidy little island lies in the English Channel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' reads as tidy, but here it is the old noun for cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: Alderney names both a Channel Island and the cattle breed from it, and neat is an archaic word for cattle.

indicators.note: designed means arranged to a new plan, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman has drawn up the plans for some medals.
explanation.definitionFit: A damsel is a young woman, a poetic synonym for she.

clue.text: These players are obviously not as mature

indicators.note: something that is obviously not the given words is the same letters in another order

explanation.surface: Unpaid players are plainly less grown-up than professionals.
explanation.definitionFit: Amateurs are players who take part without being paid, the opposite of professionals.

clue.text: Drug the Italian brought back from an African country

parts.note: soma is the drug of Huxley's Brave New World

indicators.note: brought back means the Italian article is read backwards

parts.note: il is the Italian word for the

explanation.surface: A drug and an Italian article are smuggled home from Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought back' turns the Italian article round; the answer is an adjective, so the definition is 'from an African country', not the country itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Somali describes a person or thing belonging to Somalia in the Horn of Africa.

parts.note: No 11 points to the answer at 11 across, the Gulf state, whose monarch carries an Islamic royal title

explanation.surface: A ruler lives at Number 11, like the Chancellor in Downing Street.
explanation.walkthrough: No 11 suggests Downing Street, home of Britain's finance minister, but it means the entry at 11 across, OMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The monarch of Oman bears this Muslim royal title, so he is the ruler living there.

indicators.note: stewing tea is churning in the pot, so these letters are churned into a new order

parts.note: the letters of my tea's taken as they stand

explanation.surface: Someone notices their tea has been left to stew in the pot.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of MY TEA'S gives the answer, and the whole clue also describes it: stewing tea gives off vapour.
explanation.definitionFit: Stewing tea is hot and full of vapour, which is what steamy describes.

definitions.meaning: weight in the sense of significance or meaning
goods brought into the country by a ship heading home

explanation.surface: A heavy load is shipped back on a cargo vessel heading home.
explanation.definitionFit: Import means importance or significance, and also goods brought in from abroad.

clue.text: Bank employee: in Paris she's central to transactions

indicators.note: central to means the French pronoun sits in the middle of the abbreviation

parts.note: Tr is an abbreviation for transactions

explanation.surface: A French woman works at a bank handling deals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'central to' places the French pronoun in the middle; Tr. is a standard dictionary abbreviation for transaction.
explanation.definitionFit: A teller is a bank clerk who takes in and pays out money at the counter.

indicators.note: racing means moving wildly, so the letters of the two words are scrambled

explanation.surface: Gulf princes love their camel racing.
explanation.definitionFit: Dromedaries are one-humped camels of Arabia and North Africa.

clue.text: Ellis, for one, is falling off

definitions.meaning: Ellis ... was the pen name of the writer of the Cadfael mysteries
dwindling away gradually, as in petering out

explanation.surface: A man called Ellis is taking a tumble.
explanation.walkthrough: Ellis Peters is the pen name of Edith Pargeter, author of the Brother Cadfael detective novels.
explanation.definitionFit: Ellis Peters was a crime novelist, and to peter out is to diminish or fall off.

clue.text: This traditional value can be criticised

definitions.meaning: the ... value of a property was the basis of the old British local tax called the rates
to rate is an old verb meaning to scold, so something able to be scolded

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned principle is open to criticism.
explanation.walkthrough: Before 1990 British householders paid 'rates', a local tax based on a property's rateable value.
explanation.definitionFit: Rateable value was the traditional tax valuation of a property, and to rate is also to berate.

indicators.note: losing his head means the first letter of the director's first name is dropped

explanation.surface: A film director is pictured losing his head somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: Polanski's first name is ROMAN; dropping its head gives the Gulf state.
explanation.definitionFit: Oman is a country, so it answers the question where.

parts.note: long chauffeured cars known as stretches cruise down the New York avenue

explanation.surface: Actors relax and stretch out on Broadway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stretch' points to stretch limos, extra-long luxury cars.
explanation.definitionFit: Stretch limousines are extended luxury cars of the kind seen on Broadway.

parts.note: crossing a breeding line of plants or animals with another, not stepping over a mark

explanation.surface: Someone oversteps a boundary.
explanation.definitionFit: Hybridising means crossbreeding, crossing one strain or line with another.

clue.text: Desert island opening for lotus-eaters — that's reasonable!

parts.note: Iona is an island of the Inner Hebrides

indicators.note: opening for means the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Leaving the island of the lotus-eaters would be the sensible thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desert island' looks like one idea but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Rational means guided by reason, a synonym for reasonable.

parts.note: bread is slang for money, so this is a folding holder for banknotes

explanation.surface: A question about storing a loaf in its wrapper.
explanation.definitionFit: A notecase is a wallet, which holds money or bread in slang.

definitions.meaning: religious communities such as Benedictines that nuns join
to book a place or item is to reserve or commission it

explanation.surface: Nuns are keen on certain books.
explanation.definitionFit: Religious orders are communities nuns belong to, and to order is to book or reserve.

definitions.meaning: the glamour model Katie Price worked under this name
the Hashemite kingdom in the Middle East

explanation.surface: A celebrity model has her own little kingdom.
explanation.walkthrough: Katie Price was a famous British glamour model known as Jordan.
explanation.definitionFit: Jordan was the stage name of a British model and is also a Middle Eastern kingdom.

clue.text: Would they issue stardust in Hollywood?

definitions.text: Would they issue stardust in Hollywood?

parts.words: Would they issue stardust in Hollywood?
parts.note: stardust read as the dust or ashes of film stars after they are burned

explanation.surface: A question about where Hollywood's glamour comes from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stardust' suggests glamour, but means the ashes of dead stars.
explanation.definitionFit: Crematoria are places where bodies are burned, giving ashes that are dust.

clue.text: Music can attract tourists initially in 11

parts.note: Mus is an abbreviation for music, as in degree titles

indicators.note: initially means taking the first letter of each of the three words before it

explanation.surface: Music can draw visitors to a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in 11' points to 11 across, OMAN, whose capital is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Muscat is the capital city of Oman, so it is a place in the country at 11.

clue.text: Garden trailer is attached to horse

indicators.note: attached to means the next word follows on after the horse

parts.note: an Arab is a breed of horse

explanation.surface: A trailer in the garden is hooked up to a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trailer' suggests a vehicle but means a trailing plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Arabis, or rock cress, is a low trailing plant grown in rock gardens.

definitions.meaning: a follower of the revolutionary Trotsky
an old word for an old woman

explanation.surface: A revolutionary woman with a title.
explanation.definitionFit: Trot is slang for a Trotskyist and an archaic word for an old woman.

parts.note: arch read literally: the central stone at the top of an arch that locks the rest in place

explanation.surface: Something of supreme importance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arch' as in arch-enemy suggests chief, but it is the curved structure.
explanation.definitionFit: A keystone is the central wedge-shaped block at an arch's crown, and figuratively the most important part.

parts.note: undercover read as under a roof: a covered gallery of slot machines

explanation.surface: Something offers secret entertainment for spies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'undercover' suggests spying but means under a roof.
explanation.definitionFit: An amusement arcade is a covered passage or hall full of games.

indicators.note: exotic means strange and foreign, so the letters are rearranged into an unfamiliar order

parts.note: the letters of a crab's taken as they stand

explanation.surface: A crustacean has a foreign allure.
explanation.definitionFit: A scarab is a beetle-shaped amulet worn as a lucky charm in ancient Egypt.

indicators.note: in means the letters lie inside the run of the next two words

explanation.surface: A man in a hut becomes a tennis sensation.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter Nissen designed the Nissen hut, a curved corrugated-iron shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: Nissen was the engineer who gave his name to the prefabricated hut.
